name: Saul Rosner
home: the blocks north of the port
life: Saul gave up taking fares on stormy evenings long before he gave up driving. His family interpreted each little concession as a promise of a larger one. This time he wants the decision remembered as his own. Wednesday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Saul can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I can name the color of each light with my eyes closed. My daughter says this is exactly the trouble. I want to be the one who hands the keys across.
appearance: Saul has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Look for tightly curled gray hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an olive canvas jacket with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. In conversation Saul squares up pieces of paper while thinking. Saul still wears the soft peaked cap that kept sunlight off the cab mirror.
personality: Saul is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Saul loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To decide where and when to hand the car keys across.
family: Hamish Baxter is Saul’s younger cousin. Saul remembers the birthdays. Hamish asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A play in a pocket*, Hamish says, “I had ten lines. The listener cried after the first two and asked if we could wait.”
connections: Pam Ravel (former driving pupil). They change places in the cab for a final ride over a route both know by smell.
